config.title: @scope

intro.title: @scope
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage with a navigation bar and a main content section to learn how to use the CSS @scope rule. You will learn the core concept of scoping styles to specific parts of your HTML, which helps prevent CSS conflicts and makes your code more maintainable. The main technology involved is the CSS @scope at-rule, which allows you to limit the reach of your selectors to a particular DOM subtree. By the end, you'll understand how to apply styles that only affect elements within a defined scope, keeping your styling organized and predictable.
intro.usecase: The @scope rule is essential for managing CSS specificity in complex component-based interfaces. Developers use it to isolate styles within specific UI sections like dashboard panels, nested form components, or modular card layouts without affecting global styles. For example, in a settings panel with multiple toggle groups, @scope prevents checkbox styles from leaking into other parts of the application. This pattern is particularly valuable in design systems where reusable components need encapsulated styling rules.

objectives: Apply the @scope rule to isolate CSS styles within a specific DOM subtree.
Construct a scoped style block that targets elements only within a defined root boundary.
Configure the @scope rule with both a root selector and a scoping limit to control style inheritance.
Manipulate CSS specificity by using @scope to override global styles without increasing selector weight.
Integrate @scope with existing CSS to create modular, maintainable component styles.
Implement scoped styles that prevent CSS rules from leaking out of their intended container.
Update a stylesheet by replacing nested selectors with @scope for clearer style encapsulation.

steps.title: Introduce the @scope at-rule syntax
steps.instruction: Inside the <style> element, add an @scope rule with a scope root selector of `.scoped-section` and a scope limit selector of `.regular-section`.
steps.hint: The @scope rule starts with '@scope' followed by parentheses containing the root and limit selectors separated by 'to'.
steps.seedCode:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
    <title>Scope Demo</title>
    <style>
        /* Add CSS rules here */
        @scope (.scoped-section) to (.regular-section) {
            
        }
    </style>
</head>
<body>
    <main>
        <!-- Add a <section> with class 'scoped-section' and a <div> with class 'regular-section' here -->
    </main>
</body>
</html>
steps.expectedOutcome: The @scope rule is added with the correct syntax, ready for adding scoped styles in the next step.
successCriteria: An @scope rule exists with `.scoped-section` as the scope root and `.regular-section` as the scope limit.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an @scope rule, but check the selectors. It should be `@scope (.scoped-section) to (.regular-section)`.
steps.feedbackWrong: The @scope rule is missing or has incorrect syntax. Remember: `@scope (root-selector) to (limit-selector) { }`.
